study.trial_id: Yu 2015 Dalian liraglutide vs metformin vs sitagliptin
study.notes: STUDY: 24 week randomised open label parallel three arm trial at the Endocrinology Department of Zhongshan Hospital, Dalian University, recruitment March 2013 to November 2014; 75 overweight or obese adults (BMI 25 or more) with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and no previous glucose lowering treatment randomly assigned to liraglutide (0.6 mg for one week then 1.2 mg once daily, 1.8 mg if needed), metformin or sitagliptin; Table 1 analyses 24, 26 and 25. The liraglutide against METFORMIN contrast is extracted; the sitagliptin arm is a DPP-4 inhibitor comparator under decision D-X7 and is deliberately not entered, because entering it would put the same liraglutide arm in the pool twice. SOURCE: the article text (proxy capture in the packet) carries the results narrative but its tables are behind 'Click to view' links; Tables 1 to 3 were read on 16 October from the publisher's open table page http://www.jofem.org/tables/jem304wt.htm with the Chrome extension and written to work/fulltext/companion/yu2015_jem304w_tables1_3.txt, which the numbers check runs against. CONVENTION: the Table 2 'mean change from baseline' column is an unsigned MAGNITUDE, so the direction of every row here is read from the baseline and 24 week columns of the same table (HbA1c, fasting glucose, HOMA-IR and leptin fall, HOMA-B and adiponectin rise) and the signs are written accordingly. The magnitudes differ by 0.1 from the difference of the rounded arm means in four cells (HOMA-IR liraglutide 2.6 against 2.7, HOMA-B 7.5 against 7.4 and 7.9 against 7.8, leptin metformin 1.2 against 1.3), which is what independently rounded per patient means produce, and the printed magnitudes are used. UNITS: leptin is printed as ng/dL and adiponectin as ug/dL, a hundredfold below the physiological range for this population, so the labels are wrong while the magnitudes are right; the percent scale is unaffected because the denominator is the baseline from the same table in the same unit. The printed pairwise p values are post hoc corrected for three comparisons and are recorded, while the standard error of every row comes from the two arm change SDs, as the route requires; the two agree in direction and rank (adiponectin uncorrected t 2.92 against the printed 0.027, HbA1c t 3.53 against 0.005). pct_weight_change minus 2.49 computed by the session: liraglutide lost 4.8 kg and metformin 2.6 kg (Table 2), a difference of minus 2.2 kg over the n weighted baseline weight (88.7*24 + 88.2*26)/50 = 88.44 kg, 100*(-2.2)/88.44 = -2.49. prespecified_endpoint TRUE: the paper states the study was designed to investigate glycaemic control, weight, the insulin resistance indices and the serum adipokines leptin and adiponectin. industry_funded left empty: the captured text carries no funding, sponsor or conflict statement. Total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, fasting insulin, C peptide and hsCRP have baselines in Table 1 but no 24 week value in Table 2, and the narrative reports only that they improved without reaching significance, so they are listed as reported without usable variance

rows.notes: Table 2 HbA1c: liraglutide 8.8 (1.0) to 7.1 (0.7), magnitude 1.7 (0.5); metformin 8.7 (0.7) to 7.5 (0.6), magnitude 1.2 (0.5); both within arm p < 0.001, pairwise liraglutide vs metformin p = 0.005
Table 2 fasting blood glucose: liraglutide 9.3 (1.6) to 7.1 (0.7), magnitude 2.2 (1.1); metformin 9.3 (0.9) to 7.7 (0.8), magnitude 1.7 (0.6); pairwise p = 0.117

Table 2 HOMA-IR: liraglutide 5.8 (2.4) to 3.1 (1.0), magnitude 2.6 (1.6); metformin 5.3 (2.1) to 3.7 (1.4), magnitude 1.7 (1.0); pairwise p = 0.054; the printed magnitude 2.6 is 0.1 from the difference of the rounded arm means

Table 2 HOMA-B: liraglutide 49.3 (16.6) to 56.7 (17.7), magnitude 7.5 (9.2), a RISE; metformin 45.2 (18.4) to 53.0 (20.9), magnitude 7.9 (9.8), also a rise; pairwise p = 0.998, so beta cell function improved equally in both arms

Table 2 leptin: liraglutide 28.4 (9.2) to 26.5 (7.7), magnitude 1.9 (2.5), within arm p = 0.001; metformin 29.7 (5.6) to 28.4 (5.3), magnitude 1.2 (4.9), within arm p = 0.219; pairwise p = 0.892, so the between arm leptin difference is small and uncertain despite the significant within arm fall. The unit is printed ng/dL and the magnitudes are physiological as ng/mL

Table 2 adiponectin: liraglutide 6.5 (2.2) to 8.2 (1.0), magnitude 1.7 (1.5), a RISE, within arm p < 0.001; metformin 6.3 (1.6) to 6.5 (1.2), magnitude 0.2 (2.1), within arm p = 0.565; pairwise p = 0.027. The unit is printed ug/dL and the magnitudes are physiological as ug/mL

json.design: randomised open label parallel three arm (liraglutide, metformin, sitagliptin), 24 weeks
other_markers: the sitagliptin arm contrasts (LvsS) for every marker above

rob.justification: d1 some_concerns: randomly assigned is stated but no sequence generation, concealment or baseline imbalance testing beyond a column of NS is described. d2 high: open label, with an injected agonist against two oral drugs and weight among the outcomes. d3 some_concerns: 75 were enrolled, one was excluded for gastrointestinal side effects, one was lost to follow up and three withdrew, while Table 1 analyses 24, 26 and 25, which sums to 75, so the analysed set and the withdrawals cannot both be as printed. d4 low: laboratory assays of standard analytes. d5 low: the adipokines and the insulin resistance indices are stated design aims of the study and all of them are reported

doubts: the Table 2 change column is unsigned, so every sign here is derived from the baseline and 24 week columns
the analysed n of Table 1 (24, 26, 25) sums to the 75 enrolled although the text reports one exclusion, one loss to follow up and three withdrawals
leptin and adiponectin unit labels (ng/dL and ug/dL) are a hundredfold below the physiological range; the percent scale is unaffected
the printed pairwise p values are corrected for three comparisons while the row standard errors are the uncorrected two arm quantities
no funding or conflict statement in the captured text
